pmc-10510198.creator: Sunny Maanju, Poonam Jasrotia, Surender Singh Yadav, Preeti Sharma, Prem Lal Kashyap, Sudheer Kumar, Manoj Kumar Jat, Gyanendra Pratap Singh
pmc-10510198.description: Corn-leaf aphid (CLA), Rhopalosiphum maidis (Fitch) (Hemiptera: Aphididae) is a serious economic pest of barley worldwide. pmc-10663438.title: Experiences of Family Caregivers Caring for Patient with Alzheimer’s Disease: A Hermeneutic Phenomenological Study
pmc-10663438.creator: Evelyn Hemme Tambunan, Idauli Simbolon
pmc-10663438.description: Introduction: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) becomes one of the diseases that greatly increased in the older adult population. Family caregivers play an important role in caring for family members who suffer from AD. The aim of this study was to illuminate the meaning of family caregivers’ lived experiences caring for a family member with AD from the perspective of an Indonesian.

pmc-11470129.title: Multi-scale analysis of urban forests and socioeconomic patterns in a desert city, Phoenix, Arizona
pmc-11470129.creator: Zhe Wang, Chao Fan, Xiang Que, Felix Haifeng Liao, Xiaogang Ma, Hui Wang
pmc-11470129.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Understanding the relationship between various socioeconomic factors and urban forest structure is essential for directing resources to ensure equitable distribution of green space. Through a case study of a desert city, i.e., Phoenix, AZ, this study provides a novel application of Multiscale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR) in which we explore the spatially variable relationships between a wide array of socioeconomic indicators and urban forest attributes.

pmc-11635609.title: Case report: Cerebral syphilitic gumma: a case retrospective report of eight cases
pmc-11635609.creator: Jun Liu, Wenjun Zhang, Qiuhua Jiang, Qianliang Huang, Xinyun Ye
pmc-11635609.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundCerebral syphilitic gumma (CSG), a rare manifestation of neurosyphilis, presents characteristics akin to intracranial tumors, often leading to clinical misdiagnosis.ObjectiveThis study aimed to summarize the clinical experience in diagnosing and treating CSG.Materials and methodsThe present study conducted a retrospective analysis of clinical data, encompassing the baseline characteristics, clinical presentation, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis of eight patients with CSG who were treated and diagnosed by our institution.ResultsThe median age at the initial diagnosis was 57.5 years, comprising six males and two females.

pmc-12571885.title: Leveraging active learning-enhanced machine-learned interatomic potential for efficient infrared spectra prediction
pmc-12571885.creator: Nitik Bhatia, Patrick Rinke, Ondřej Krejčí
pmc-12571885.description: Infrared (IR) spectroscopy is a pivotal analytical tool as it provides real-time molecular insight into material structures and enables the observation of reaction intermediates in situ. However, interpreting IR spectra often requires high-fidelity simulations, such as density functional theory based ab-initio molecular dynamics, which are computationally expensive and therefore limited in the tractable system size and complexity.

pmc-12613567.title: Advances in PLGA-based polymeric nanocarriers for colorectal cancer therapy: overcoming chemoresistance through controlled delivery strategies

pmc-12613567.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is among the most prevalent malignancies globally, with a notably higher incidence in men. Despite the availability of multiple chemotherapeutic options, clinical efficacy remains limited due to poor drug solubility, restricted intestinal absorption, rapid systemic clearance, and multidrug resistance.

pmc-13231856.title: A scoping review on cardiometabolic risk factors among Pacific Island populations and implications on future research in the region
pmc-13231856.creator: Tristan V C Paulino, Bwenaua Biiri, Elizabeth Matisoo-Smith, Anna L Gosling
pmc-13231856.description: Indigenous populations in the Pacific are disproportionately burdened by cardiometabolic diseases compared to other populations, yet understanding of the underlying factors contributing to these health disparities remains limited. A combination of genetic and non-genetic risk factors contributes to cardiometabolic disease outcomes, but current reviews involving Pacific Island peoples are limited by geographical and demographic constraints.
